chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: Coffee, whiskey and diet
summary: Smitty has coffee, and Danny and Milt recall how whiskey kept them going and that poor diet shortened lives like King Oliver's.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: [POURING] Have a little coffee there, Danny, while you're talking. You don't have to stop a thing. Here, Smitty.
Thank you. In New Orleans a man have to have his little coffee every now and then.
Yeah. At one time he would have had whiskey.

Or we would have had a bottle. But when you get up to a certain age, you have to watch your diet. That diet business, huh? If they had had a diet in the early Thirties, King Oliver and all of them people probably would have been living. But they didn't have the proper diet.
That's right. Well, we kept working nights on that whiskey, Danny, for a long time.
I'm telling you. That whiskey lots of times kept you going, too.
Because you didn't give a damn. You'd say, 'Okay, well, this is rough, but we're going to make this.'
Yeah. We had enough youth and strength in our body to accept that shock ...(?)... Ah, I'll take me a little taste of the grape every now and then.

I don't want to leave it completely. I'm trying to think about the times that you and I would sit up with a few good whiskeys, and it would last us about an hour. And in ...(?)... before we'd go to the theatre, you'd
sit there drinking, and you'd have to have another one to take to the hotel that night.
